newsitem.title: UK: Marks & Spencer bounces on positive comment.
newsitem.headline: Marks & Spencer bounces on positive comment.

text.p: Shares in Marks & Spencer Plc rebounded in early trading on Wednesday from yesterday's sharp decline sparked by a negative reaction on the retail group's first half results.

Traders said press comment on the results helped steady nerves over the stock, with some citing the influential Financial Times Lex column, which said M&S's growth prospects justified its slight premium rating to the rest of the sector.
"The Lex column was reasonably warm about them today," said one senior trader. The stock was up 6-1/2p at 643-1/2 by 0834 GMT, after yesterday 26p fall to a three-month low.
Analysts said yesterday's drop in the shares was probably overdone but reflected a genuine surprise at the impact of rising costs as M&S recruits an extra 2,000 staff.

"It was a bit overdone yesterday," said Nick Bubb, analyst at MeesPierson. "Assuming the staff increase is a one-off, it will blow away about 40 million stg this year but by 1997-8 we should see sales growing faster than costs again."

Bubb said he had cut his current-year forecast for M&S pre-tax profit by 50 million stg to 1.11 billion stg -- with 10 million of the downgrade representing lower-than-expected food sales -- and cut his forecast for the year after by 25 million stg to 12.75 billion.
"M&S has complained about naive analysts but I don't think they did a good job informing the market of the increase in costs," he said.
Yet Bubb said the retail sector in general should remain in favour in the run-up to Christmas and with the budget later this month expected to include some small tax reductions.
"M&S gave a bit of a jolt to sentiment but I don't think its a disaster for the stores sector," he said. "It's still right to be overweight ahead of the budget and Christmas."
